newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS -U.S. bond vols up as futures stay buoyant.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -U.S. bond vols up as futures stay buoyant.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond volatilities climbed Wednesday as futures extended the previous session's sharp advance.

The two-day rally that began Tuesday on news of weaker than expected U.S. employment costs in the first quarter carried through to today's session, reinforced by technical strength and optimism about a U.S. budget pact. News the gross domestic product grew 5.6 percent in the first quarter, exceeding forecasts, had only a mildly negative impact, traders said.
Implied volatility for June bonds was quoted at 8.85 percent late in the session, up from Tuesday's settlement of 8.75 percent, but below the opening level of 9.00 percent.
September was unchanged from the previous session at 9.10 percent after rising to 9.20 percent on the opening.

Several good-sized transactions were executed in bond options, floor sources said. Early in the session, a Wall Street dealer firm bought 2,000 June 108-00/109-00/110-00 call "Christmas tree" spreads. Later, the same firm bought 2,000 June 107-00/108-00 put spreads.
Two Japanese brokerage firms each bought 1,000 June 110-00 calls, and a U.S. house sold 1,000 June 109-00 calls while also buying 2,000 June 109-00/110-00 call spreads.
June bond futures ended off the session highs at 109-09, up 11/32, and September Eurodollars settled unchanged at 93.875.

Volatilities for Eurodollar options also rose, with September up 0.3 point, at 11.50 percent, and December up 0.2 point, at 12.80 percent, late in the session. Short-dated midcurve volatilities were 0.5 point higher at 17.50 percent in September and steady at 16.60 percent in December.

Market participants will focus Thursday on the National Association of Purchasing Management's April survey, forecast at 53.6. Friday is the April jobs report, with nonfarm payrolls predicted up 211,000 and the unemployment rate seen unchanged at 5.2 percent.
